title: Family of man shot by police seeks probe: Lawyer says they just want answers
article: The family of 18-year-old Keyvan Tabesh, shot to death by Port Moody police July 14, is demanding an external investigation into their son's death.
"The family is in deep shock and incredible grief," their lawyer, former B.C. police complaint commissioner Don Morrison, said yesterday. "They just want answers and information at this point."
Morrison said the family does not believe a probe by Port Moody police will get to the truth.
In a statement, Tabesh's father, Nasser, said the family wants Morrison to be able to cross-examine the officer at a coroner's inquest "to help us understand what really happened."
The family held a prayer service at Tabesh's gravesite Friday night. Morrison said he and his wife attended the vigil along with at least 30 of Tabesh's relatives and friends.
"There was a lot of disbelief . . . the grief was palpable," Morrison said.
He said Nasser Tabesh, a retired surgeon, and his wife, former chemist Forough Jabalamei, brought their family to Canada from Iran two years ago.
The parents have two other children: Kamyar is an engineering student at UBC and his sister Rita is a microbiolgist.
"They never, in their wildest imaginations, contemplated their son would be . . . killed by \[the police\]," said Morrison.
"The father . . . saved thousands of lives in the war between Iran and Iraq, and one of the questions he has is, 'Why God? Why me? I've saved so many lives and now this happens.' "
Keyvan Tabesh was killed by a 25-year veteran of the Port Moody force after he allegedly lunged at the officer with a machete.
Earlier, two women told police Tabesh's car bumped their parked car from behind, and that Tabesh got out and smashed in their back window with a machete.
An on-duty plainclothes officer in an unmarked car later spotted Tabesh pulling into a cul-de-sac.
It is not known whether he identified himself as a police officer before fatally shooting Tabesh and injuring his friend, Amir Aghaei.
B.C.'s chief coroner has yet to announce whether an inquest will be held into Tabesh's death.
